concepts.name: Statutory Origin and Legal Framework of RRBs
key_dimensions: RRB Act 1976 vs. Narasimham Committee recommendation (1975) — cause vs. legislation

concepts.name: Ownership Structure and Capital Shareholding Pattern
key_dimensions: Tripartite ownership: Central Government (50%), Sponsor Bank (35%), State Government (15%) — exact percentages are UPSC traps
Post-2015 amendment: allowance for private shareholding up to 49% without disturbing public character
Difference between 'sponsor bank' ownership and 'parent bank' — RRB is NOT a subsidiary
Recapitalization burden sharing ratio between Centre, State, and Sponsor Bank

concepts.name: Role and Mandate of Sponsor Banks
key_dimensions: Sponsor bank functions: training staff, subscribing to share capital, providing managerial support
Sponsor bank ≠ controlling authority — RBI and NABARD retain regulatory roles (common confusion)
Sponsor banks are scheduled commercial banks (predominantly nationalized banks)
Liability of sponsor bank for RRB losses — limited vs. unlimited liability distinction

concepts.name: Regulatory and Supervisory Architecture of RRBs
key_dimensions: RBI as regulator for banking functions vs. NABARD as supervisor — dual oversight trap
NABARD's inspection powers under Section 35(6) of Banking Regulation Act
Central Government's power to supersede RRB Board vs. RBI's powers over commercial banks — difference

concepts.name: Geographical Jurisdiction and Area of Operation
key_dimensions: RRBs operate in notified districts — originally single district, now multi-district post-amalgamation
Intra-state vs. inter-state operation — RRBs cannot operate across state boundaries (key constraint)
Difference from cooperative banks' area restriction vs. RRB's district/state restriction
'Local feel, commercial bank efficiency' — original design philosophy and how amalgamation altered it

concepts.name: Target Clientele and Priority Sector Lending Mandate
key_dimensions: Original mandate: small and marginal farmers, agricultural labourers, rural artisans — Section 2 of RRB Act
Priority sector lending targets for RRBs: 75% of ANBC vs. 40% for commercial banks — critical difference
Sub-targets within priority sector — agriculture (18%), weaker sections (15%) for RRBs
Drift from original mandate post-liberalization — RRBs allowed to lend to non-target groups, controversy

concepts.name: Amalgamation and Consolidation of RRBs
key_dimensions: Phase I amalgamation (2005–06) under Vyas Committee recommendation — reduction from 196 to 82
Subsequent phases reducing RRBs further — current number (~43) vs. original 196 is a factual trap
Rationale: viability, scale economies, NPA reduction — vs. criticism of losing local character
Amalgamation within same sponsor bank and same state — two binding conditions

concepts.name: Financial Viability and NPA Profile of RRBs
key_dimensions: Historically loss-making nature — recapitalization schemes (2010–11, 2015–16, 2021–22)
Gross NPA ratio of RRBs vs. SCBs vs. cooperative banks — comparative vulnerability
Reasons for higher NPAs: waiver culture, priority sector exposure, weak recovery mechanism
Profitability turn-around post-amalgamation — data used in Mains answers

concepts.name: RRBs vs. Cooperative Banks: Structural and Functional Comparison
key_dimensions: RRBs: government-sponsored, commercial bank DNA; Cooperatives: member-owned, state-regulated — fundamental difference
Regulatory body difference: RRBs under RBI+NABARD; Urban Cooperatives under RBI; Rural Cooperatives under state registrar+NABARD
Deposit insurance: both covered under DICGC — common correct statement that traps students
Credit delivery overlap in rural areas — why both coexist and their complementarity vs. competition

concepts.name: RRBs and Financial Inclusion Mandate
key_dimensions: RRBs as BC (Business Correspondent) channel and their own branch network — two modes
Role in PMJDY account opening — RRBs among top performers in rural zero-balance accounts
Aadhaar-linked DBT disbursement through RRBs — last-mile connectivity function
Limitation: technology gap vs. SFBs (Small Finance Banks) as rival financial inclusion vehicle

concepts.name: NABARD's Refinance and Developmental Role for RRBs
key_dimensions: NABARD provides short-term, medium-term, and long-term refinance to RRBs — types and purposes
NABARD's Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF) — RRBs' shortfall routed here
NABARD's capacity building and MIS support — beyond just refinance (often ignored)

concepts.name: Capital Adequacy and Prudential Norms Applicable to RRBs
key_dimensions: CRAR norms for RRBs: 9% minimum (same as SCBs) — but implementation timeline was different
Whether Basel III norms apply to RRBs — they do NOT in full; simplified prudential norms apply
Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) and Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) applicability to RRBs — same as SCBs
Recapitalization to meet CRAR — Centre:State:Sponsor Bank = 50:15:35 ratio mirrors ownership

concepts.name: Interest Rate and Deposit Mobilization Framework
key_dimensions: RRBs can offer higher interest rates than sponsor banks — original provision to attract rural deposits
Post-deregulation: interest rate autonomy for RRBs on deposits above 1 year — partial deregulation
Savings bank rate still regulated — difference from term deposit rate freedom
Competition with Post Office Savings Schemes in rural areas for deposits

concepts.name: Technology Adoption and CBS Implementation in RRBs
key_dimensions: Core Banking Solution (CBS) rollout — NABARD-supported, completed by 2016 across all RRBs
RuPay Kisan Card and mobile banking — RRBs' digital product suite vs. commercial banks
NACH (National Automated Clearing House) integration for DBT — operational significance

concepts.name: Narasimham Committee Recommendations and RRB Evolution
key_dimensions: Narasimham Committee I (1991): recommended conversion of RRBs into commercial banks or merger with sponsor banks — radical proposal
Narasimham Committee II (1998): consolidation and recapitalization rather than merger — shift in stance
Vyas Committee (2001 & 2004): business development and amalgamation model — implemented
Difference between Committee recommendations and actual government policy — UPSC loves this gap

concepts.name: RRBs and Agricultural Credit Delivery: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme
key_dimensions: RRBs as one of three institutional channels for KCC (alongside commercial banks and cooperatives)
KCC coverage through RRBs — share in total KCC accounts issued

concepts.name: Governance Structure and Board Composition of RRBs
key_dimensions: Board composition: Chairman (appointed by Central Govt.), directors nominated by Centre, State, and Sponsor Bank
Chairman's qualifications and appointment process — Central Government role vs. sponsor bank influence
Corporate governance reforms post-2015 Amendment Act — independent directors provision
Supersession of RRB Board: Central Government power (not RBI, not NABARD) — a key trap

concepts.name: RRBs' Role in Government Schemes and Direct Benefit Transfers
key_dimensions: PM-KISAN, MGNREGS, NSAP disbursements through RRB accounts — operational conduit function

Challenge: seeding Aadhaar with accounts held in RRBs — lower completion rate vs. PSBs
Social security schemes (PMSBY, PMJJBY, APY) enrollment through RRBs — Jan Suraksha schemes

concepts.name: Listing and Capital Market Access for RRBs
key_dimensions: RRBs currently NOT listed on stock exchanges — unlike PSBs and some cooperative banks
Post-2015 amendment: enabling provision for equity dilution to raise capital from markets
Debate on IPO of RRBs: financial autonomy vs. loss of rural development focus
Contrast with Small Finance Banks which ARE listed — SFB vs. RRB capital access comparison

concepts.name: One State–One RRB Vision and Current Restructuring
key_dimensions: 'One State–One RRB' proposal under Union Budget 2019–20 and subsequent policy push
Current status: amalgamation ongoing — number reduced but not yet one per state in all cases
Arguments for: economies of scale, better capital, unified management; Against: loss of local identity
